correctness.rationale: The independent bounded enumeration retained exactly the orientations with outdegree two at every vertex and applied the integer Walsh transform in the stipulated ascending-edge coordinates. It reproduced all 15 signed multiplicities, rank 6336, nullity 10048, gap 4, the ±60 extremes, and exactly the two specified families among the 91 two-edge tests. Thus the condition number is 15 and the inverse norm 1/4. Complementing every reversal bit explains the 8192 odd-weight zeros; subtracting gives 1856 even-weight zeros. The cut-space argument uses differences of two Eulerian reversal words, or a translate by one fixed Eulerian word, not the assertion that the ascending-label orientation is Eulerian. The independent inverse transform of the nonzero support reproduced the full kernel histogram and its absolute numerator sum 71936, divided by 16384. A real or complex projection conjugated by any translation maps into the range and fixes it; the average therefore still projects and has no greater norm. Commutation with translations forces the unique Fourier support-indicator projection, whose counting-measure endpoint norms both equal its kernel's absolute sum (281/64).
residual_risks: Exhaustive on this labelled graph only. Changing reference directions translates the orientation set, which can change individual multiplier signs; the check used the specified convention.

value.rationale: This is the first odd squared cycle beyond the complete-graph C5² case in the odd-cycle-square family. The independent-edge convolution is a natural refinement of two winding counts. In particular, the low-weight census isolates an offset-specific mixed-edge correlation that a uniform winding statistic does not resolve. The full spectrum distinguishes invertible modes from cancellations, and the evaluated optimal norm gives a precise test case for recovery comparisons. The value is in these graph-specific invariants, not the prior count or reuse of the Fourier method.
residual_risks: Finite benchmark only; no law of Fourier recovery or cancellation motifs at higher orders is established.
